newsitem.title: INDIA: POTENTIAL KESRI RIVALS EMERGE ON CONGRESS PANEL.
newsitem.headline: POTENTIAL KESRI RIVALS EMERGE ON CONGRESS PANEL.

text.p: Supporters of Congress party president Sitaram Kesri won most of the seats on the party's decision-making committee but three potential antagonists emerged during the weekend election, analysts said.
Kesri supporters were elected to seven of the 10 spots on the Congress Working Committee (CWC), party officials said. The panel has 20 members, 10 of whom will be appointed by Kesri at a later date.
But the election of former Maharashtra state chief minister Sharad Pawar and former cabinet minister Arjun Singh could herald a fresh power struggle within the party, analysts said.
"Both Pawar and Singh are quite capable of initiating a fresh round of struggle within the party, and the two may get support from Azad," said political scientist O.T. Mishra.

He was referring to former cabinet minister Gulam Nabi Azad, whose election was announced after 29 hours of counting at the party's 80th plenary meeting which ended on Sunday in the eastern city of Calcutta.
Former minister Rajesh Pilot, whose bid for party leadership fell well short in June, lost out to Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy in a neck-and-neck battle.
The seven official nominees who were elected were Jitendra Prasada, Madhavrao Scindia, Tariq Anwar, Ahmed Patel, Pranab Mukherjee, R.K. Dhawan and Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy.
None of the 10 represent lower castes, considered crucial by political analyts for the Congress to have a socially broad-based image.
"We will have adequate representatives of the weaker sections in the CWC when the remaining 10 members are nominated," Kesri told reporters.
